title: Hall/Van de Castle content coding
finding: Dream reports can be described with consistent content categories.
context: A descriptive coding system for dream reports.
limitation: Describing an element does not decode an individual's hidden psychological meaning.
allowed_inference: Use stable categories to compare what appears across entries.

title: Malinowski and Horton: emotional waking experiences
finding: In a diary study, incorporated waking experiences were more emotional than non-incorporated experiences.
context: 32 participants kept waking and dream diaries over 14 days.
limitation: This does not establish the meaning of a particular dream or prove a causal interpretation.
allowed_inference: Explore emotional similarities with context provided by the dreamer.

title: Wegner, Wenzlaff and Kozak: Dream Rebound
finding: Deliberately suppressing thoughts of a person before sleep increased subsequent reports of that person in dreams.
limitation: The reverse inference is not established: dream content does not prove suppression or avoidance.
allowed_inference: Ask whether a pattern relates to an already reported concern; do not diagnose repression.

title: Weinstein and colleagues: psychological need experiences
finding: Need experiences related to dream emotions; findings for specific recurring themes were mixed.
context: Studies of recurring and daily dream reports.
limitation: Particular dream themes cannot be treated as a reliable test for unmet needs.
allowed_inference: Explore feelings and situations, including counterexamples, with the user's input.

title: IASD dreamwork ethics
finding: The dreamer decides the personal significance of their dreams.
context: Professional dreamwork guidance, not an experimental study.
limitation: Personal resonance does not prove an interpretation is objectively true.
allowed_inference: Offer direct questions while respecting disagreement and uncertainty.
